title: Cap. IV open: duplex decretum — general (all believers) and singular (named from foreseen faith)
pass_a_gloss: Predestination therefore having been constituted in this manner from foresight of faith, a double decree of Predestination is established by Arminius and his followers. The prior is general, by which God decreed to receive all believers into grace for Christ's sake, and to gift the same persevering in faith with eternal life. The latter is singular, and is terminated at singular persons: By which God established to gift with eternal glory this one and that one by name, for example Peter, Paul, John, whom from eternity he foresaw would believe, and would remain in faith.
pass_b_english: With predestination thus set from foresight of faith, Arminius and his followers establish a double decree. The first is general: God decreed to receive all believers into grace for Christ's sake, and to gift those persevering in faith with eternal life. The second is singular and terminates on particular persons: God established to gift with eternal glory this one and that by name — Peter, Paul, John — whom from eternity he foresaw would believe and remain in faith.
source_text: Praedestinatione ergo hunc in modum ex praevisione fidei constituta, duplex Praedestinationis decretum ab Arminio, ejusque sectatoribus stabilitur. Prius generale est, quo Deus decrevit omnes credentes in gratiam recipere propter Christum, eosdemque in fide perseverantes aeterna vita donare. Posterius singulare est, et ad singulares personas terminatur: Quo Deus statuit hunc et illum nominatim, puta Petrum, Paulum, Johannem, quos ab aeterno praevidit credituros, et in fide permansuros, aeterna gloria donare.
